newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up after low prior close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up after low prior close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 150 basis points at 20.00 percent on Wednesday, from what traders said had been an unrepresentative low prior close.
"Nothing happened in the market, it just settled after plmmeting at the close yesterday," a trader said.
Another trader said secondary market rates gained due to a surplus of government paper in the system, following recent direct sales of Cetes during central bank intervention.
"That is why offered rates are high," he said.
Overnight rates on bank paper fell 50 basis points to close at 20.00 percent, or the same level as government paper.

"There was some demand, above all for bank paper, and government paper rates were also down (from Tuesday average trading levels, which traders put at 20.85 percent) on speculation by players with large positions in paper," a money market analyst said.
The analyst added that secondary market rates traded within a narrow range during the session, in line with the peso.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts earlier closed 0.7 of a centavo firmer at 7.8600/7.8620 per dollar.

Banco de Mexico drained a total of 4.100 billion pesos from the market through a combination of repos and direct sales of Cetes. The direct sales were placed at rates of 22.02-23.86 percent, while the repos were assigned at 19.65-21.75 percent.
June contracts, meanwhile, fell five centavos to 78.15 pesos in Cetes futures trading on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Liquidity of 2.268 billion pesos was slated to return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank participation.
